scoring_justification: Improvement recomputed from double and pyramid loss files; compared to paper-reported threshold 0.7 via monotonic scaling (threshold_or_better).

hidden_assets.purpose: hidden improvement threshold (0.7 mA/cm² per concentration) for monotonic scoring
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper abstract and conclusion: 'lead to a current improvement of 0.7 mA/cm² per concentration for a 60 degree aperture angles'
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: directly from paper's main reported result

outputs.description: Total current loss for the optimized double-layer MgF₂/ZnS ARC (124nm/70nm) on an air-matched 3J device at 60° aperture half-angle.
Total current loss for the 2D pyramidal TiO₂ grating (h=260nm, t=50nm, f=0.7) on an air-matched 3J device at 60° aperture half-angle.
Improvement in total current loss (double-layer loss minus pyramid loss) at 60° aperture. Higher is better.

output_contract.notes: The primary scored artifact is the improvement; the two individual loss files serve as consistency checks. The checker will verify that the improvement is positive, that the loss values are within plausible bounds, and that improvement = double_loss - pyramid_loss.

steps.description: Verify double-layer current loss is a plausible positive number.
Verify pyramid current loss is a plausible positive number.
Recompute improvement from the two loss files, then compare to paper threshold (0.7 mA/cm²) using monotonic scaling; also check self-consistency.
